scope: Focused r3 machine-rule deployment delta: df mount record and fresh Popen attribution/termination; prior handshake/budget/size findings carried forward, science unchanged

findings.title: Continue supervising the owned group after scientific parent exit
findings.detail: terminate_owned returns immediately when the tracked Popen parent has exited. supervise_child exits its loop when that same parent exits, then calls terminate_owned on nonzero return, so an abrupt parent exit can leave an active same-group scientific worker unsupervised. A successful parent exit with an unexpected remaining worker is also never checked. The previous unconditional owned-group cleanup handled this leader-exit path; the new attribution guard removes it. Parent death does not imply process-group death.
findings.required_change: Retain enough attributable identity for the owned session/group to inspect and clean surviving task workers even after the leader exits. Before any member/group signal verify cmdline, elapsed/create_time and cwd plus the owned session/group; never signal a reused/ambiguous group by username or numeric PGID alone. Do not mark supervision complete while attributable owned workers remain. Add a pure synthetic case with a parent that exits while its child remains alive, and verify cleanup and stopped/failure accounting without touching other work.

verified_changes: resource_check records exact df -h / /mnt/data2 /mnt/data3 with bounded subprocess timeout and keeps data2 mount/capacity requirement.
Fresh Popen bind checks exact args, cwd, create_time and own group; live-leader TERM and escalation recheck identity instead of relying on shared username.
